You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From aa8e73eed7d3084c18dd16d195748661c7e881b5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Date: Fri, 25 Mar 2022 13:30:47 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] crypto: x86/sm3 - Fixup SLS

This missed the big asm update due to being merged through the crypto
tree.

Fixes: f94909ceb1ed ("x86: Prepare asm files for straight-line-speculation")
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>
---
 arch/x86/crypto/sm3-avx-asm_64.S | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/arch/x86/crypto/sm3-avx-asm_64.S b/arch/x86/crypto/sm3-avx-asm_64.S
index 71e6aae23e17..b12b9efb5ec5 100644
--- a/arch/x86/crypto/sm3-avx-asm_64.S
+++ b/arch/x86/crypto/sm3-avx-asm_64.S
@@ -513,5 +513,5 @@ SYM_FUNC_START(sm3_transform_avx)
 
 	movq %rbp, %rsp;
 	popq %rbp;
-	ret;
+	RET;
 SYM_FUNC_END(sm3_transform_avx)
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the omission of an update to the assembly code for the SM3 cryptographic function, specifically related to the handling of straight-line speculation (SLS) in the x86 architecture. The original code used a lowercase 'ret' instruction, which was not compatible with the new requirements introduced by the SLS changes, necessitating the use of the uppercase 'RET' instruction to ensure proper function return behavior in the context of speculative execution.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>
    <text3>
    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the omission of an update to the assembly code for the SM3 cryptographic function, specifically related to the handling of straight-line speculation (SLS) in the x86 architecture. The original code used a lowercase 'ret' instruction, which was not compatible with the new requirements introduced by the SLS changes, necessitating the use of the uppercase 'RET' instruction to ensure proper function return behavior in the context of speculative execution.
